title: Shaw, Renik and Sass, Angler and environmental influences on walleye and muskellunge angler catch in Escanaba Lake
endpoint: Angler trip success and successful-trip catch rate
finding: Methods exclude water temperature because of correlated predictors. Successful-trip walleye CPUE decreases modestly with air temperature.
limitations: Air-temperature coefficients cannot be used as water-temperature response; successful-trip CPUE differs from unconditional trip success; inland lake, not pier.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Wu et al., PPAR Signaling Maintains Metabolic Homeostasis under Hypothermia in Freshwater Drum
endpoint: Metabolism and gene expression in approximately 21-g cultured fish
finding: Methods: 25 C acclimation followed by 18 or 10 C over six hours, sampled for eight days.
limitations: Juvenile/culture and acute-change context; neither winter adult inactivity nor angling response can be inferred.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Maahs, Sylvia and Weber, Effects of Length and Bag Limits on Largemouth Bass Tournament Capture and Mortality
finding: Weigh-in model includes positive water-temperature association; measurements combine 0 and 4.6-m locations.
limitations: Weigh-in is conditional on tournament rules/angler behavior and excludes culled fish. No open-pier probability, winter curve or surface-only response.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Qualich and Louison, Effects of Temperature, Air Exposure Time, and Bleeding on Post-Release Movement of Angled Channel Catfish
endpoint: Post-angling depth and acceleration, not pre-capture success
finding: Temperature did not predict post-release depth or acceleration; seasonal effects were not equivalent to feeding.
limitations: Power-plant lake and injured/released fish. No warm-water optimum or catch-response plateau established.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Reed et al., Initial insights on the thermal ecology of lake whitefish in northwestern Lake Michigan
geographicScope: Northwestern Lake Michigan and Green Bay; 2017–2018
endpoint: Archival occupied temperatures, 13 recovered tags from 400 deployments
finding: Winter occupied range 0–8 C; summer mean 10.8 C with many observations outside proposed narrow bands.
limitations: Small recovered sample; occupancy, not selection or lawful pier feeding. Broad shoulders are product judgments.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Foraging activity and habitat use throughout an annual migration of adult walleye from the Trent River in eastern Lake Ontario
geographicScope: Trent River and eastern Lake Ontario
endpoint: Adult telemetry, vertical movement and inferred foraging
finding: Cold-season behavior differs from warm-season movement; cited 21 C value describes peak growth.
limitations: Movement and modeled growth do not identify an angling optimum; migration and pier reachability differ.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Bergstedt et al., In situ determination of annual thermal habitat use by lake trout in Lake Huron
finding: Most summer occupancy was colder than laboratory preference, with strain and individual variation.
limitations: Agency abstract reviewed; fish temperature at depth differs from modeled surface temperature; no directed pier catch curve.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Michigan DNR, Largemouth bass
finding: Agency describes activity at 70–85 F and continued winter activity.
limitations: General activity band, not a measured bite plateau. Harbor cover and winter movement differ from lake-facing piers.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: USGS Fish Health Program, Yellow perch
endpoint: Agency preference and seasonal activity summary
finding: General 19–21 C preference and winter activity.
limitations: Does not justify suppressing locally supported cold spring pier catches or identify a catch-rate optimum.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Michigan DNR, Grand Haven, Muskegon and Whitehall/Montague single-pointed hook regulations
geographicScope: Named ports; Grand Haven westernmost pierhead to US 31 bridge
finding: November restriction requires one unweighted single-point hook no more than half an inch point-to-shank; jigs and spearing prohibited in the defined waters.
limitations: Applies to gear in the area, not just targeting whitefish. Regulatory scope does not prove species-specific South-Pier catch magnitude; 2026 guide must be reconciled before activation.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Wismer and Christie, Temperature Relationships of Great Lakes Fishes
geographicScope: Great Lakes and historical source-study locations
finding: PDF pages 71, 136 and 192 visually checked. Adult drum preference differs from young fish and heated-discharge observations; catfish acclimation changes preference; round-whitefish records are sparse and context-dependent.
limitations: Historical compilation, not independent adult pier angling data. Underlying studies not all retrieved; no numeric bite probabilities.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Wisconsin DNR, Guide to the Future project summary
endpoint: Guided fly-angling, skill-corrected catch rate and shaded noon water temperature
finding: PDF page 22 visually checked. Smallmouth catch rate increased over the sampled temperature range.
limitations: River/method transfer only; no identified optimum or declining warm limb, no winter sample sufficient for a fitted annual response.
readingScope: Original full page/PDF relevant sections reviewed; agency abstract where stated

title: Michigan DNR, 2026 Michigan Fishing Regulations
endpoint: Hook-and-line seasons and gear restrictions; printed pages 12, 13, 17, 21, 31
finding: Bass catch-and-immediate-release is year-round unless waters otherwise closed. Lake trout MM 6-8, including Manistee, is open all year. Grand Haven November 1-30 requires one single-pointed unweighted hook, point-to-shank no greater than half an inch, from westernmost pier head to US-31 bridge.
limitations: Legal permission is not catch evidence; current access closures remain separate. Lake-side walleye rules must not be extended upstream. Pages 12, 13, 21, 31 visually inspected after local PDF extraction.
readingScope: Full original document relevant sections read

title: Arielle Breen, Fishing report shows local conditions, best methods
geographicScope: Manistee North Pier; secondary reprint of June 26, 2024 DNR report
finding: Reprint specifies North Pier drum on the harbor side; links the original DNR bulletin B_3a521c4.
limitations: The original DNR report says only the pier. North attribution is the newspaper wording, not an agency-confirmed side; the reprint is not an independent catch event.
readingScope: Full original document relevant sections read

title: Harman et al., Effect of elevated embryonic incubation temperature on the temperature preference of juvenile lake and round whitefish
geographicScope: Laboratory shuttle-box; twelve-month juvenile round whitefish
endpoint: Thermal selection after developmental incubation treatments, DOI 10.1093/conphys/coad067
finding: Round-whitefish groups were 55-62 mm, 1.19-1.71 g. Group mean upper avoidance 15.11-15.80 C; lower avoidance 13.04-13.73 C after common rearing at 15 C.
limitations: Juvenile acclimated preference is not adult pier feeding or bite response; does not validate an adult 6-10 C plateau. No numerical profile is fitted to these values.
readingScope: Full original document relevant sections read
